walkthrough_label: Example Patient D - the deteriorating patient (watch the numbers change)
reason_answer: I have had tummy pain for three days.

presentation.summary: Usman, 34, arrives at 14:00 after three days of tummy pain he 'tried to sleep off'. The numbers change over the next two hours: the trainee must notice the trend.

history.answer: Three days of tummy pain. I tried to sleep it off.
Fever and sweats since yesterday; no urine symptoms.
Ibuprofen from the shop for the pain.
No anaesthetic problems in the family.
Toast two days ago; sips of water today.

observations.note: Infection, coping. Workup started. Book NEWS2 2.
No fluids or antibiotics given yet. Heart faster, BP lower, breathing faster, fever higher. Book NEWS2 5.
Sepsis with poor circulation: EMERGENCY. Book NEWS2 10.
If nobody acts: septic shock, near collapse. The book prints NEWS2 16; the table gives 17 (ISS-0016, owner decided: use 17).
After the correct action: BP 108/64 and HR 112 after fluids; lactate falls to 2.4; urine flowing.

examination.finding: At 14:00: tender in the lower right tummy with guarding.
At 14:45: sweaty; tummy now tender everywhere and rigid: suggests perforation with spreading peritonitis.

problems.label: Sepsis with poor circulation (NEWS2 5 then 10)
problems.why: A rising heart rate, falling BP and rising temperature are one trend: perforated appendix with sepsis.
expected_actions: Look at him: sweaty, tummy rigid
Sepsis bundle: blood cultures, lactate, IV antibiotics, fluid bolus with re-check, oxygen per protocol, urine measurement

problems.label: Antibiotics and fluids within 1 hour for the high-risk tier
problems.why: NICE NG253: high-risk tier needs antibiotics and fluids within 1 hour.
expected_actions: Give antibiotics and fluids by the clinician's order

problems.label: Perforated appendix: urgent source control
problems.why: Surgery removes the source once resuscitation has started.
expected_actions: Request urgent CT if the senior wants it (escort and monitor)
Emergency call at 15:15: senior surgeon and anaesthetist
Handover with lactate, fluids, antibiotic time, NEWS2, kidney injury, aspiration risk

decisions.prompt: At 14:45 NEWS2 is 5 (was 2). What do you do?

options.text: Go and look at him; call for urgent senior review; start the sepsis bundle (cultures, lactate, IV antibiotics and a fluid bolus, oxygen if needed, urine measurement); request urgent CT if the senior wants it
options.consequence: Matches the book (NEWS2 5 to 6: urgent review; NG253).

options.text: Wait for the next routine observations
options.consequence: The trend is the warning; waiting costs time.

options.text: Give paracetamol and re-check in an hour
options.consequence: Treats the number, not the sepsis.

options.text: Emergency call: senior surgeon and anaesthetist now; critical care aware; ABCDE; a second drip, more fluid boluses with re-checks, antibiotics if not yet given, catheter; theatre urgently after resuscitation starts
Send him for CT first before treating

decisions.prompt: If he is confused, how is consent handled?

options.text: If he still has capacity: a brief but complete discussion; if not, the senior follows the emergency route per local protocol

correct: 14:45: notice the trend; look at him; call urgent senior review; sepsis bundle
15:15: emergency call; ABCDE; antibiotics within the hour; source control
After treatment BP 108/64, HR 112, lactate 2.4; theatre urgently

incorrect.shows: By 15:15 NEWS2 10; by 15:45 BP 82/48, confused, NEWS2 17

missed: Antibiotics given at 15:55 (70 minutes late) in the missed-trend path
recovery: Recognise late, call the senior, start the bundle, stabilise, go to theatre

debrief.related: Heart rate, BP, breathing and fever are one story
debrief.trigger_escalation: NEWS2 5 or more with infection; NEWS2 7 or more
debrief.remember: Look at the trend, not one number; sepsis criteria were met at 14:45
